keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 macro nature photo in a garden. A thin brown twig with a few green leaves crosses the top of the frame. A second thin green stem rises from the bottom right of the frame. Under one leaf near the top middle of the frame hangs one round fluffy golden-orange silk egg sac, wrapped in a loose net of fine silk, attached to the leaf by a few silk threads. The egg sac is about one twelfth of the frame width wide. A few loose single silk threads run from the twig down to the stem. The middle of the frame between them is open. Soft out-of-focus green garden background, soft morning light, sharp focus. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the twig, the leaves, the stem, the silk threads, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The egg sac is now torn open and empty in the same place. Just below it, hundreds of tiny newly hatched spiderlings form one tight round ball on the silk threads. Each spiderling is bright yellow with a small black patch on its abdomen. The ball is about one eighth of the frame width wide. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the twig, the leaves, the stem, the empty egg sac, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The ball of spiderlings is gone. In the middle of the frame, between the twig and the stem, there is now one small round orb web, about one third of the frame width wide. One small yellow-brown spiderling with a dark patch sits in the center of this small web, head down. It is about one twentieth of the frame width long. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the twig, the leaves, the stem, the empty egg sac, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The web and the spider in its center are now bigger, with the same center point: a round orb web about two thirds of the frame width wide. The spider in the center, head down, is now about one tenth of the frame width long, light brown, with the first small white spots on its round abdomen. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the twig, the leaves, the stem, the empty egg sac, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. A large complete round orb web now fills most of the frame, with the same center point, anchored to the twig and the stem, with many neat spiral threads. In its center sits an adult female garden cross spider, head down, with a large round brown abdomen marked with a white cross made of spots, and banded brown legs. Its body is about one sixth of the frame width long. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the twig, the leaves, the stem, the large orb web, the old empty egg sac, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The center of the web is now empty. The same adult female spider, with the same size and the same white cross, now sits on the underside of the leaf next to the old empty egg sac, beside one new round fluffy golden-orange silk egg sac wrapped in a loose silk net. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.
